property_summary: The supportsInterface function returns true for a given interfaceId if and only if it matches IAccessControl interface or ERC165's supportsInterface returns true for it.
If cancel is called with a non-pending operation id, it should revert; otherwise it should succeed.
For any bytes4 interfaceId, calling supportsInterface on C returns the same value before and after any cancel call.
After any cancel call, supportsInterface returns true for IAccessControl interfaceId.
For every bytes4 interface ID, the value of c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) is always equal to (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId).
A call to supportsInterface with the IAccessControl interface ID returns true.
The cancel function reverts for any operation id that is not pending.
After any sequence of operations, calling supportsInterface with the IAccessControl interface ID returns true.
After cancel of any operation, supportsInterface returns the same as before cancel.
Calling supportsInterface with the IAccessControl interface ID returns true immediately after construction.
After canceling an operation, its timestamp should be zero (not pending).
The timelock operations can be scheduled and then canceled only when the caller has the PROPOSER_ROLE.
Calling hasRole for a role on an address after canceling an operation that was proposed by that address must return the same value as before canceling.
cancel(id) does not change the PROPOSER_ROLE membership of the caller.
After canceling a scheduled operation, the EXECUTOR_ROLE membership of the timelock contract itself (address(this)) is unchanged.
Cancel always succeeds when called by a proposer with a pending operation id.
The cancel function reverts when called with an operation id that is not pending, regardless of the caller's role.
The return value of hasRole(role, account) is always false when account is address(this) and role is not bytes32(0).
The cancel function reverts when called by the contract itself (address(this)) with a non-pending operation id, regardless of whether the caller has the default admin role.
Calling cancel with bytes32(0) never reverts when called by the contract itself
Cancelling a scheduled operation should succeed when called by an account with the PROPOSER_ROLE, and fail when called by an account without that role.
Calling cancel() on a pending operation returns false for isOperationPending() after cancel, and the operation's timestamp becomes 0.
An account with the PROPOSER_ROLE can cancel a pending operation, but an account without that role cannot.
After calling cancel(id) for a pending operation, getTimestamp(id) must be 0.
After cancel(id) returns without reverting, the operation's timestamp must be 0.
After scheduling an operation, calling cancel with a non-PROPOSER role must revert; but the mutant allows it for any caller.
If the caller is not the proposer, calling cancel must revert; but the mutant's always true hasRole allows cancel for any caller.
When cancel is called with an id corresponding to a pending operation, it must revert if the caller does not have the PROPOSER_ROLE.
After executing an operation, calling cancel with the same operation id must revert.
cancel(bytes32) must revert when called by any address that does not have the PROPOSER_ROLE.

The cancel function reverts when the caller lacks the required role (PROPOSER_ROLE) and the admin role of PROPOSER_ROLE is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, which holds for the reference but fails in the mutant where getRoleAdmin always returns 0x00.
After cancelling an operation, the operation's timestamp becomes 0 (i.e., the operation no longer exists), regardless of the caller's role.
getRoleAdmin returns the admin role set by _setRoleAdmin, not a constant.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the admin role that was set for that role, which for non-DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE roles is DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.
For any role, getRoleAdmin returns the stored admin role, not a constant 0x00.
After calling cancel (which requires PROPOSER_ROLE), the caller cannot renounce the PROPOSER_ROLE of another account.
After a successful cancel operation, the caller can still renounce their own PROPOSER_ROLE.
After a cancel operation, a proposer who is not the timelock contract cannot revoke their PROPOSER_ROLE by calling renounceRole, but can still renounce an arbitrary role.
Cancelling an operation should not allow an account to renounce a role they do not hold.
After a cancel operation, an account that never renounced their PROPOSER_ROLE should still have the role if they never called renounceRole.
The cancel function should only revert when the operation id is not pending; if it is pending, it should succeed, otherwise it should revert.
For any operation id, isOperation returns true if and only if the cancel function does not revert when called with that id.
cancel should succeed if and only if isOperation returns false on the operation id after the call, meaning the operation is still pending before cancel.
cancel reverts if and only if isOperationPending returns false for the given id.
For any operation id, isOperation returns true if and only if the cancel function does not revert when called with that id.

For any operation id, if its timestamp equals _DONE_TIMESTAMP and it's pending, then calling cancel should revert; in the reference, cancel reverts when isOperationPending returns false (i.e., timestamp == _DONE_TIMESTAMP), but the mutant incorrectly treats that as pending.
If an operation id has timestamp exactly equal to _DONE_TIMESTAMP, then calling cancel should revert.
For any operation id with getTimestamp(id) < _DONE_TIMESTAMP, calling cancel should revert.
If an operation's timestamp is exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP, then isOperationPending returns false and cancel reverts.
For any operation id, if its timestamp is exactly _DONE_TIMESTAMP, then isOperationPending returns false and cancel should revert.
For all bytes32 arguments, calling isOperationPending returns true on a scheduled operation that has not been cancelled or executed (i.e., getTimestamp(id) > _DONE_TIMESTAMP).

For any bytes32 id, after scheduling an operation, cancel reverts if isOperationPending(id) is false; in P, cancel succeeds when timestamp == _DONE_TIMESTAMP (i.e., not pending), but M's isOperationPending returns true incorrectly.
For any bytes32 id, after scheduling an operation with a delay and then calling cancel, isOperationPending(id) returns false
After an operation is executed (isOperationDone returns true), isOperationPending must return false.
For a cancelled operation, isOperationPending should return the same as isOperationDone (i.e., false) but due to the bug, it incorrectly returns true.
If isOperationPending returns false for an id, then cancel should revert; otherwise cancel should succeed.
If isOperationPending returns false for an id, cancel should revert; otherwise cancel should succeed.
If isOperationPending(id) returns false, then cancel(id) must revert; if it returns true, cancel(id) must succeed.
For any operation id, isOperationPending(id) should return false if and only if getTimestamp(id) == _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
After a successful cancel of an operation, isOperationPending returns false and getTimestamp returns _DONE_TIMESTAMP.
cancel only reverts when isOperationPending returns true
For any id, cancel(id) reverts exactly when isOperationPending(id) returns false.
If an operation is pending, then cancel(id) should succeed and the operation should no longer be pending.
After cancel(id) reverts, isOperationPending(id) returns the same value as before.
For any id, cancel(id) reverts if and only if isOperationPending(id) returned true before the call.
The cancel function only succeeds when the operation is pending (isOperationPending returns true).
After canceling an operation, it is no longer operation pending (isOperationPending returns false).
A new, non-existent operation (with id = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(block.timestamp))) has isOperationPending returning false.
An operation that was never scheduled cannot be pending (isOperationPending returns false).
Before calling cancel, isOperationPending returns true; after cancel, it returns false.
isOperationReady returns true only when getTimestamp(id) > 1 and getTimestamp(id) <= block.timestamp
After cancel, isOperationReady returns false for the cancelled operation id.
After cancel, isOperationDone returns false for the cancelled operation id.
For any operation scheduled with a block number in the past, isOperationReady returns true exactly when the operation is ready to execute (i.e., when its timestamp is > 1 and <= block.timestamp).
After cancel, the operation timestamp should be 0, so isOperationReady should return false for the cancelled operation id.
For any scheduled operation id, isOperationDone returns false until the operation is executed.
After canceling an operation, isOperationDone returns false.
For any operation id, immediately after cancel(id) reverts, isOperationDone(id) returns false.
If cancel(id) succeeds (does not revert), then after the call isOperationDone(id) returns false.
For any operation id, if isOperationDone(id) returns true, then it must be that isOperationPending(id) returns false.

After cancel(bytes32) is called, getTimestamp(id) should return a value that is not equal to the original timestamp, and specifically should return 0 if cancel did not revert, but the mutant always returns 0 even before cancel.

After a successful cancel, getTimestamp(id) should return _DONE_TIMESTAMP (1), but the mutant's getTimestamp always returns 0, so the invariant is that cancel either reverts or the timestamp after cancel is 1.
After scheduling an operation and then calling cancel, getTimestamp returns 0 if cancel succeeded, but the mutant always returns 0 even before cancel.

After scheduling an id, the timelock returns a timestamp greater than 1, but after cancel succeeds it returns 0. The mutant always returns 0, breaking the invariant that a scheduled operation returns a non-zero timestamp.
After scheduling and then successfully canceling an operation, getTimestamp returns 0, but the mutant always returns 0 even for scheduled operations.
getTimestamp returns the stored timestamp for any operation id, which equals block.timestamp + delay when scheduled, and is not equal to block.timestamp.
After calling cancel(id), getTimestamp(id) returns 0, indicating the operation is no longer pending.
After scheduling an operation with schedule() and then canceling it, isOperationPending() returns false.
After scheduling an operation and waiting for the delay to pass, getTimestamp returns block.timestamp + delay for the reference but block.timestamp for the buggy version.
The getTimestamp function returns a stored timestamp that is at least block.timestamp for any operation that is pending or ready, and returns 0 for an operation that has been cancelled.
The getMinDelay() function must return the current minimum delay (which is set in the constructor and can be updated later), not a constant 0.
The getMinDelay() return value must be accessible and non-zero when a non-zero delay was set in the constructor.
After a successful execute, the operation's timestamp is set to DONE_TIMESTAMP (1).
The minimum delay returned by getMinDelay() must be non-zero when the contract was constructed with a non-zero minDelay parameter.
The return value of getMinDelay() must equal the value passed as minDelay in the constructor.
After any call to cancel with an arbitrary id, if the operation was pending before the cancel, getTimestamp(id) should return 0.
The getMinDelay function returns the minimum delay value set in the constructor without modification.
After canceling any operation, the operation's timestamp is always 0 or unchanged if it was not pending.
The getMinDelay function always returns the value set in the constructor.
The getMinDelay function returns the value set by the constructor (0) – a constant – which the reference satisfies but the mutant breaks by returning 1.
The getMinDelay() return value must be less than type(uint256).max.
After scheduling an operation, cancel(id) will fail if the operation timestamp is not greater than the done timestamp.
A scheduled operation with delay of _minDelay must be ready after its timestamp passes, but cancel should revert if the operation is pending.
After scheduling an operation with delay equal to getMinDelay(), the schedule timestamp is exactly block.timestamp + delay, and cancel(id) succeeds before the operation becomes ready.
After scheduling an operation, the timestamp returned by getTimestamp(id) must be greater than _DONE_TIMESTAMP and greater than block.timestamp plus getMinDelay().
